VERSO — four directions for the verdict screen

Same real scan in all four: a US bread whose label declares potassium bromate. Every claim and citation on screen comes from the live API, so this is a fair comparison of treatment, not of content.

Pick one and I'll build the Compare screen — the cross-market feature — in that language, then the full screen set.

The constraint they all answer to: docs/naming.md commits Verso to pointing without accusing. A direction that reads as an accusation undermines the legal posture in docs/claim-templates.md.

A · THE DOSSIER  ← my recommendation

Axis: evidence-led, editorial.
Newsreader serif + Archivo + Plex Mono, ink on document paper.

The headline IS the finding, stated as fact. The score is small and quiet; the record is the hero. Citations sit in mono directly under each claim at equal typographic weight — nothing hidden behind 'view source'.

Why: it looks like something that gets things right, which is what you are actually selling. Furthest from Yuka's colour-score register.

Tradeoff: the least immediate in an aisle. Reading, not glancing.

B · THE INSTRUMENT

Axis: scientific, measured.
IBM Plex Mono + Plex Sans, dark instrument panel, amber readout.

Signature move: the score is a measurement with its uncertainty shown. The hatched region of the gauge is what we have NOT measured — evidence coverage rendered honestly instead of buried in small print.

Why: makes the suppression rule a visible virtue rather than an apology, and reads as precision.

Tradeoff: dense and cold. Risks feeling like a tool for experts, not a shopper.

C · THE SIGNAL

Axis: signage, immediate.
Archivo 900 at poster scale, flat signal red, no gradients.

The count is the hero — readable at arm's length in bad supermarket light, in under two seconds. This is the one that gets screenshotted and shared.

Why: maximum immediacy and virality.

Tradeoff — and it is real: the register drifts toward accusation. A 118px red '2 countries ban it' is a verdict on a company, not a citation. Beautiful, and the direction most likely to attract a letter.

D · THE PASSPORT

Axis: jurisdiction as the native metaphor.
Instrument Serif + Archivo, security-paper guilloche, rubber stamps, a machine-readable strip.

Each jurisdiction is a physical mark, so 'banned in two countries, pending in a third' is legible at a glance without shouting. The ingredient is the subject of a record; markets endorse or refuse it.

Why: the most distinctive of the four, and the only one where Compare is native rather than an extra tab.

Tradeoff: the strongest metaphor, so the most that can go wrong at scale — 400 ingredients of stamps could tire.
